title: Vertebrates
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Group real or pictured Kenyan animals: tilapia, frog, chameleon, crocodile, hen, ostrich, bat, goat, dolphin. The child checks a short list of body features (skin covering, how young are born, where they live) before naming a group.

skills.key_step: The child gives the shared features of vertebrates (a backbone and a skeleton inside, a skull, a body in head, trunk and often limbs or fins) and does not judge by size, legs or a hard outside.

floor.prerequisite: Can sort animals by whether they have a backbone.
floor.question: Does a snake have a backbone?

representations: a table of features ticked for five animals
steps: All vertebrates have a backbone and a skeleton inside.
They have a skull that protects the brain.
Some are warm-blooded (mammals, birds), others are not (fish, amphibians, reptiles).
Test hard cases: snake, tiny frog, crab.

board.do: Draw a fish skeleton with the backbone and skull.
Wait for the child to say the brain.
Ask whether a crab has a skeleton like this inside.

listen_for: it is too small to be a vertebrate
misconceptions.ask: Does a tiny frog have a backbone?
misconceptions.repair: Size does not decide; the backbone does.

misconceptions.ask: What long bone do we find in a fish?
misconceptions.repair: Fish and snakes have backbones without legs.

listen_for: the hard shell is the backbone
misconceptions.ask: Is the crab's hard part inside or outside its body?
misconceptions.repair: A shell is outside; a backbone is inside.

misconceptions.ask: Why does a lizard lie in the sun in the morning?
misconceptions.repair: Fish, amphibians and reptiles change temperature with their surroundings.

checks.question: Name two features all vertebrates share.
checks.answer: a backbone and a skull (a skeleton inside)

checks.question: Is a lizard warm-blooded like a goat?
checks.answer: No: its temperature changes with its surroundings

skills.key_step: The child puts a vertebrate in one of five groups (mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish) by its features, not by where it lives or whether it flies.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the shared features of vertebrates.
floor.question: Does a hen have a backbone?

representations: odd cases: bat, ostrich, dolphin, crocodile
steps: Feathers: bird. Fur and milk: mammal.
Dry scales, eggs on land: reptile.
Moist skin, young in water: amphibian.
Gills, fins, scales in water: fish.

board.do: Draw five columns: mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, fish.
Write bat, ostrich, crocodile, frog, dolphin under them.

board.say: It flies. Which group is it in?

board.do: Wait for the child to decide.
Ask the child to place the rest.

misconceptions.ask: Does a bat have feathers or fur? Does it feed its young on milk?

listen_for: it lives in water so it is a fish
misconceptions.repair: Living in water does not make an animal a fish.

misconceptions.ask: Is the chameleon's skin dry and scaly or moist?
misconceptions.repair: Reptiles have dry scales; amphibians have moist skin.

listen_for: an ostrich cannot fly so it is not a bird
misconceptions.repair: Feathers make a bird, flying or not.

listen_for: it lays eggs so it is a bird
misconceptions.ask: Do crocodiles and fish lay eggs?
misconceptions.repair: Many groups lay eggs; feathers mark a bird.

checks.question: Which group is a crocodile in?
A dolphin lives in the sea and feeds its young on milk. Which group is it in?

skills.key_step: The child matches a body feature (fur, feathers, dry scales, moist skin, gills, milk) to the group it marks, and uses more than one feature for hard cases.

floor.prerequisite: Can name the five groups of vertebrates.
floor.question: Name the group with feathers.

representations: a feature card for each group
a two-way table: feature by group
steps: Look at the body covering first.
Then how the young are born and fed.
Then how it breathes: lungs or gills.
Check with a second feature before deciding.
contexts: a snake skin found on a path

board.do: Draw a table: covering, breathing, young.
Fill in a row for the goat.
Point at an empty row for the bat.
Wait for the child to say fur.
Ask the child to fill in the bat's row.

misconceptions.ask: Does a bat or a butterfly have feathers?
misconceptions.repair: Feathers, not wings, mark a bird.

misconceptions.ask: Where does an adult frog sit when it is not in the pond?
misconceptions.repair: Amphibians live in water when young and on land and in water as adults.

misconceptions.ask: Look at the bat's wing: feathers or skin?
misconceptions.repair: Bats have fur and wings of skin.

misconceptions.ask: How does a dolphin feed its young?
misconceptions.repair: Milk for the young marks a mammal, on land or in water.

checks.question: Which feature is found only in birds?
An animal has moist skin and lays eggs in water. Which group is it in?
